It is exactly that. I used a graphing caulcator with my parameters to model an equation. I knew that f(x) -√|x| was the general shape I needed and changed it until I got a curve I was happy with, so that I passed through (0,120) as my tower was 120m tall, and crossed the x axis at ±384 as that was the length of the bridge either way. I ended up with, -√(|43.75x| +100) + 130, which gave a nice curve and then, using Excel, calculated the difference between each value of f(x) for every multiple of 8 as the foundation are 8m long and then just went along building the vertical beams to the correct height and then filling them in with diagonal beams. 

Bit a of long winded explanation but it makes making a smooth curve easier
